newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Kazakh dealers see T-bill yields roughly unchanged.
newsitem.headline: Kazakh dealers see T-bill yields roughly unchanged.

text.p: Yields on Kazakh Treasury bills, kept low by stable demand and balanced money supply, are likely to remain roughly unchanged at auctions next week, dealers said on Friday.
The Finance Ministry will auction 600 million tenge of 12-month discount MKM T-bills on July 28 and the same amount of three-month paper on July 29.

Three-month bills edged up to 13.56 percent on Tuesday from 13.44 percent at the last auction on July 15, while the yield on 12-month paper eased to 15.35 percent on July 15 from 15.74 percent at the previous auction on July 2.

Most dealers said they expected yields to remain stable next week. "We do not expect anything extraordinary...the situation on the (T-bill) market is quiet amid stable demand. We will bid for the same yields as at previous auctions," said Asan Buranbayev of Zhilstroibank.
Lyudmila Pogulyayeva of ABN AMRO Bank Kazakhstan said "I think yields will be roughly on the same level, the more so as we do not expect very large redemptions next week."
Murat Altynbayev, head dealer at Bank TuranAlem, said a seasonal let-up in activity and smaller investment orders were another reason for the slow market.
He added that the National Bank and the Finnace Ministry had been successful in stabilising the money supply by regularly issuing short-term National Bank notes.
Other dealers agreed. "If there is no note issue next week, there can be a slight, virtually insufficient decrease in yields," Pogulyayeva said.

Buranbayev said yields still might move up slightly. "At the end of each month there is usually a slight rise in yields, because banks need funds to make necessary reserve requirement payments imposed by the National Bank," he said. "But this time, it would be really a minimal rise."
